#~run tool mos6502-export
#~run modeling_2026 054c9c35
#~run board apple_ii
#~run mix typical
#~run page_cross 0.1
#~run branch_taken 0.6
#~run overlap yes
#~model sha256=c29a1770cfd292fbe3f9120d9bb6a492f6e6f5e5426add5c18d6d1602fc1145a lines=118 name=mos6502.dc
#~ title MOS 6502 (1975) -- the chip, and an Apple II-class board, as a floor
#~ # The 6502's datapath as the MCS6500 hardware manual's block diagram draws it:
#~ # four internal 8-bit buses -- DB (data), ADL and ADH (address low and high)
#~ # and SB (special) -- with the registers that read and drive them, the
#~ # control section above, and the 40 pins below. On the board, the CPU and
#~ # the video scanner share the RAM by clock phase: the scanner reads it in
#~ # phase 1, the CPU in phase 2 (Sather, Understanding the Apple II), so the
#~ # video steals nothing from the CPU.
#~ # Ids are unique and say what a thing is (6502-SB, BRD-ZP); names are the
#~ # type, and label the boxes.
#~ # Figures at 1 MHz, from the 6502 model in Modeling_2026
#~ # (full_stack/mos_6502/topology.json, each figure with its source there):
#~ #   external bus: one byte every cycle, every cycle -- 8 Mb/s (Tier A,
#~ #     MCS6500 hardware manual); the CPU drives it in phase 2 only
#~ #   RAM: phase 1 to the video, phase 2 to the CPU -- 16 Mb/s in all
#~ #   internal bus: one transfer a clock phase -- 16 Mb/s (Tier C: an estimate
#~ #     from the two-phase clock, not a measurement)
#~ #   latency: one clock phase, 500 ns, a bus (Tier C)
#~ # Each internal bus is drawn as wide as the datapath it runs across, and
#~ # met along its length: the registers drop straight onto it (w= and
#~ # cables=bus, viewer 1.53.0 or later).
#~ # The viewer moves traffic over this; it does not run 6502 instructions --
#~ # tools/mos6502-export brings what the Modeling_2026 model works out (CPI,
#~ # MIPS, each board's effective clock) onto these elements. Try: shift-click
#~ # X and the accumulator (TXA, over SB), or the ROM and the instruction
#~ # register (an opcode fetch, through predecode); or a test flow from RAM to
#~ # the video and another from RAM to the CPU, each at 8 Mb/s -- both get it.
#~ # A route is the fewest hops over cables that carry both ways, so a load
#~ # into the accumulator is drawn over AC/DB backwards: the chip loads A only
#~ # from SB (SB/AC), over the SB/DB pass. The links below say which way each
#~ # control drives.
#~ # Its cables carry traffic both ways, so the input data latch (in only) and
#~ # the data output register (out only) are drawn as one data bus buffer:
#~ # two boxes would split every byte between them.
#~ dc SYS dir=x name=system
#~   package CPU dir=y id=6502 name="6502, 40-pin DIP"
#~     control CTL dir=x id=6502-CTL name="control"
#~       node PREDECODE id=6502-PREDECODE name="predecode register" role=fetch +switch
#~       node IR id=6502-IR name="instruction register" role=ir
#~       node PLA id=6502-PLA name="decode ROM (PLA)" role=decode +switch
#~       node RCL id=6502-RCL name="random control logic" role=control
#~       node TIMING id=6502-TIMING name="timing (T-states)" role=timing
#~       node INT id=6502-INT name="interrupt logic" role=interrupt
#~       node CLK id=6502-CLK name="clock generator (phi1, phi2)" role=clock
#~     buses BUSES dir=y id=6502-BUSES name="internal buses"
#~       node ADH id=6502-ADH name="address bus high (ADH)" role=bus +switch latency=500ns w=209 cables=bus
#~       node ADL id=6502-ADL name="address bus low (ADL)" role=bus +switch latency=500ns w=209 cables=bus
#~       node SB id=6502-SB name="special bus (SB)" role=bus +switch latency=500ns w=209 cables=bus
#~       node DB id=6502-DB name="data bus (DB)" role=bus +switch latency=500ns w=209 cables=bus
#~     datapath DP dir=x id=6502-DP name="datapath"
#~       node ABH id=6502-ABH name="address register high" role=addr +switch
#~       node ABL id=6502-ABL name="address register low" role=addr +switch
#~       node PCH id=6502-PCH name="PC high" role=reg
#~       node PCINC id=6502-PCINC name="PC incrementer" role=pcinc +switch
#~       node PCL id=6502-PCL name="PC low" role=reg
#~       node DBB id=6502-DBB name="data bus buffer (input latch DL, output register DOR)" role=latch +switch
#~       node CONST id=6502-CONST name="ADH constants (page 00, page 01)" role=const +switch
#~       node S id=6502-S name="stack pointer" role=reg
#~       node ALU id=6502-ALU name="ALU (A in, B in, adder hold)" role=alu
#~       node A id=6502-A name="accumulator" role=reg
#~       node Y id=6502-Y name="index Y" role=reg
#~       node X id=6502-X name="index X" role=reg
#~       node P id=6502-P name="status register" role=reg
#~     pins PINS dir=x id=6502-PINS name="pins"
#~       node AH id=6502-A8-15 name="address pins A8-A15" role=pins +switch
#~       node AL id=6502-A0-7 name="address pins A0-A7" role=pins +switch
#~       node D id=6502-D0-7 name="data pins D0-D7" role=pins +switch
#~       node CPINS id=6502-CTLPINS name="control pins (R/W, SYNC, RDY, IRQ, NMI, RES, phi0-2)" role=ctlpins
#~   board BRD dir=y id=BRD name="board"
#~     node ADEC id=BRD-ADEC name="address decoder" role=adec
#~     node DBUS id=BRD-DBUS name="data bus" role=sysbus +switch latency=500ns
#~     node MUX id=BRD-MUX name="RAM address multiplexer" role=mux +switch
#~     ram RAM dir=x id=BRD-RAM name="RAM, 48 KB"
#~       node ZP id=BRD-ZP name="zero page (0000-00FF)" role=memory
#~       node STACK id=BRD-STACK name="stack page (0100-01FF)" role=memory
#~       node MAIN id=BRD-MAIN name="RAM (0200-BFFF)" role=memory
#~     node ROM id=BRD-ROM name="ROM (D000-FFFF)" role=memory
#~     node IO id=BRD-IO name="I/O (C000-CFFF)" role=io
#~     node VIDEO id=BRD-VIDEO name="video scanner" role=video
#~ net bus gbps=0.016
#~ net pin gbps=0.008
#~ net ext gbps=0.008
#~ net ram gbps=0.016
#~ net ctl gbps=0.001
#~ # The internal buses, wired as the visual6502 netlist names its datapath
#~ # controls (nodenames.js: ADL/ABL, ADH/ABH and dpc0-dpc43; the bus names are
#~ # Hanson's, from his block diagram). Each line lists the controls that make
#~ # its connections -- X/Y "drive Y from X" -- so which way each one carries is
#~ # here even where a cable cannot say it.
#~ #   ADH: ADH/ABH; PCH/ADH, ADH/PCH; DL/ADH; SB/ADH (a pass, both ways);
#~ #        0/ADH0, 0/ADH1-7 (the constants that make page 00 and page 01)
#~ link bus id=6502-ADH id=6502-ABH|6502-PCH|6502-DBB|6502-SB|6502-CONST
#~ #   ADL: ADL/ABL; PCL/ADL, ADL/PCL; S/ADL; ADD/ADL, ADL/ADD; DL/ADL
#~ link bus id=6502-ADL id=6502-ABL|6502-PCL|6502-S|6502-ALU|6502-DBB
#~ #   SB:  Y/SB, SB/Y; X/SB, SB/X; S/SB, SB/S; ADD/SB, SB/ADD; AC/SB, SB/AC
#~ #        (through the decimal adjust); SB/DB (a pass, both ways)
#~ #   DB:  DL/DB; DB/ADD, not-DB/ADD; AC/DB (drive only: A loads from SB);
#~ #        PCL/DB; PCH/DB; P/DB, DB/P (Hanson); DB into DOR
#~ #   the PC increment: PCL/PCL, PCH/PCH, carry from PCL to PCH
#~ link bus id=6502-PCINC id=6502-PCL|6502-PCH
#~ # To and from the pins.
#~ link pin id=6502-ABH id=6502-A8-15
#~ link pin id=6502-ABL id=6502-A0-7
#~ link pin id=6502-D0-7 id=6502-DBB|6502-PREDECODE
#~ # The opcode's way in, and the control it becomes.
#~ link ctl id=6502-PREDECODE id=6502-IR
#~ link ctl id=6502-PLA id=6502-IR|6502-TIMING|6502-RCL
#~ link ctl id=6502-RCL id=6502-TIMING|6502-INT|6502-CLK|6502-CTLPINS
#~ # The board: addresses end at the decoder, which picks a device; data moves
#~ # on the data bus, and the RAM is shared with the video.
#~ link ext id=BRD-ADEC id=6502-A8-15|6502-A0-7
#~ link ext id=BRD-DBUS id=6502-D0-7|BRD-ROM|BRD-IO|BRD-MUX
#~ link ext id=BRD-MUX id=BRD-VIDEO
#~ link ram id=BRD-MUX id=BRD-ZP|BRD-STACK|BRD-MAIN
#~end model
